sentences.text: Nanshiungosaurus was a large therizinosaurid dinosaur estimated to reach nearly 5 meters in length and weigh between 600 and 907 kilograms.
This animal is differentiated by stocky posterior cervical vertebrae that feature opisthocoel centra, meaning the back of each bone is concave.
It was a pot-bellied creature with a strong build, stout hindlimbs, and a foot that functioned with four toes despite having only three visible.
A well-preserved axis vertebra measures 13.5 cm in length and possesses platycoelus centra, which are slightly concave at both ends.
The seventh and eighth cervical vertebrae are the longest in the neck, with their centra measuring 18 cm in length.
The pelvis of Nanshiungosaurus had an opisthopubic structure where the pubis and ischium bones were fused and directed backwards.
The ilium was stocky and featured an extremely well-developed, elongated preacetabular process but completely lacked a postacetabular process.
The genus Nanshiungosaurus was formally described by Dong Zhiming in 1979.
The type species, Nanshiungosaurus brevispinus, was discovered in 1974 and formally described in 1979.
Fossil remains were found in 1974 during an expedition at the Nanxiong Basin in Guangdong Province.
The holotype specimen, cataloged as IVPP V4731, consists of twelve cervical, ten dorsal, six sacral, and the first caudal vertebrae along with a nearly complete pelvis.
Nanshiungosaurus was a bulky high-browser that shared its habitat with various oviraptorosaur species.
Its ecosystem included the tyrannosaurid Qianzhousaurus, the sauropod Gannansaurus, and sparse remains of the hadrosaurid Microhadrosaurus.
The fauna also included nanhsiungchelyid turtles, squamates like Chianghsia and Tianyusaurus, and the crocodilian Jiangxisuchus.
Early research on therizinosaurs was complicated by sparse remains that led some to interpret them as prosauropod dinosaurs.
A 2010 analysis by Zanno concluded that the family Nanshiungosauridae was invalid and a synonym of Therizinosauridae.
The parent group of Nanshiungosaurus is Therizinosauridae.
It was one of the last therizinosaurids to exist before the end of the Cretaceous period.
A second species, Nanshiungosaurus bohlini, was described in 1997 based on remains found in 1992, but its validity is unsupported.
It is debated whether Nanshiungosaurus bohlini belongs to the genus, as the original describers provided no evidence or argumentation to support the assignment.
There is a scientific consensus that the specimen Nanshiungosaurus bohlini is no longer considered related to the main genus Nanshiungosaurus.
